title: The Second Vow
premise: Ghostwriter Tamsin Dunmore has spent a decade anonymously answering letters for her reclusive mentor, and one correspondent—signing only 'W'—has become the closest thing she has to a confidant. When W turns out to be Jonah Vale, the disgraced former judge who just moved in next door while writing his own memoir, Tamsin is hired to ghost it, forcing her to hide that she knows him better than he knows himself. As they fall for each other through drafts and half-truths, Tamsin uncovers evidence that could clear Jonah of the corruption charges that ended his career—but exposing it means revealing her identity and risking both their hearts. In the end she chooses to be seen: she testifies alongside him at the reopened inquiry, signs her own name to his book's final chapter, and they marry quietly with their found family of letter-writers as witnesses.
about_author: Noor Underhill is a former court stenographer who turned to fiction after transcribing one testimony too many. She writes from a coastal cottage where she still answers every letter by hand.

chapters.title: The Letters She Never Signed
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Establishes her invisible life ghostwriting memoirs and secretly answering her mentor's fan mail, including ten years of letters to 'W.' Beat: loneliness disguised as contentment.

chapters.title: The Man Next Door
chapters.summary: Jonah moves into the neighboring cottage; Tamsin recognizes his handwriting instantly but says nothing. POV alternates via his returned mail. Beat: panic masked as curiosity.

chapters.title: A Commission in Confidence
chapters.summary: A publisher hires Tamsin to ghost Jonah's memoir under NDA. She accepts, telling herself it's professional. Beat: the trap closes gently.

chapters.title: First Sessions
chapters.summary: Their recorded interviews begin; Jonah is guarded, prickly about the trial that ruined him. Tamsin steers him with knowledge only 'W' should have. Beat: dangerous intimacy.

chapters.title: What W Knew
chapters.summary: Jonah mentions the anonymous correspondent who kept him sane in prison; Tamsin nearly confesses, then deflects. Her POV. Beat: guilt sharpening into fear.

chapters.title: The Sister Who Stayed
chapters.summary: Introduce Priya, Jonah's estranged sister and local baker, who becomes Tamsin's friend without knowing whose ghost is writing next door. Beat: found family begins forming.

chapters.title: Drafts and Half-Truths
chapters.summary: Late-night working sessions blur professional lines; almost-kiss interrupted by a subpoena notice on Jonah's door. Beat: hope undercut by threat.

chapters.title: The Case File
chapters.summary: Tamsin finds discrepancies in the old trial transcript while fact-checking—a witness who recanted off-record. Beat: justice outside the law becomes personal.

chapters.title: Priya's Kitchen
chapters.summary: Warm interlude: Priya feeds them both, unknowingly reuniting siblings' stories. Tamsin watches Jonah laugh and realizes she loves him. Beat: tenderness before the fall.

chapters.title: The Recanting Witness
chapters.summary: Tamsin tracks down Marisol Vega, who admits she was paid to lie. Marisol will only speak if protected. Beat: moral weight lands on Tamsin alone.

chapters.title: Almost Honest
chapters.summary: Jonah confesses to Tamsin that W's letters saved his life—and that he's falling for his ghostwriter. She almost tells him everything. Beat: the confession withheld.

chapters.title: Rival Memoir
chapters.summary: Tamsin's other client, celebrity financier Dorian Ashe, publishes a memoir smearing Jonah; her ghostwritten prose is weaponized against him. Beat: complicity exposed to herself.

chapters.title: The Unmasking
chapters.summary: Jonah discovers a draft page in Tamsin's handwriting matching W's letters. He confronts her; she admits everything—the letters, the silence, the lies. Beat: heartbreak as climax approaches.

chapters.title: Ashes of the Draft
chapters.summary: Jonah ends the book and the friendship; Tamsin, devastated, decides to act anyway—not for him, but because it's right. Beat: identity chosen over safety.

chapters.title: Marisol's Statement
chapters.summary: Tamsin shelters Marisol with Priya's help, gathering affidavits and following money trails Dorian left. Beat: the found family becomes an underground network.

chapters.title: Dorian's Leverage
chapters.summary: Dorian threatens to expose Tamsin's ghostwriting breaches unless she buries the evidence. Beat: the cost of speaking named.

chapters.title: The Second Vow
chapters.summary: Tamsin gives a sworn statement to the inquiry under her own name, surrendering anonymity and career in one breath. Beat: climax—she risks the whole heart.

chapters.title: What the Inquiry Found
chapters.summary: Hearing scenes; Marisol testifies, the bribe trail surfaces, and Jonah's conviction is vacated pending retrial. He learns Tamsin testified first. Beat: vindication arriving too late to feel like victory.

chapters.title: The Last Chapter, Signed
chapters.summary: Jonah asks Tamsin to finish the memoir—with her name beside his. They write the ending together, honestly this time. Beat: reconciliation through collaboration.

chapters.title: Dorian Falls
chapters.summary: Publication of their co-authored book triggers investigation; Dorian's empire cracks. Tamsin declines credit publicly, takes it privately. Beat: justice completed, ego released.

chapters.title: Small Hours
chapters.summary: Quiet chapter: Jonah proposes not with a ring but with a letter, ten years' worth finally answered in person. Priya caters. Beat: love made ordinary and real.

chapters.title: Epilogue: Return Address
chapters.summary: One year later, married, they run a letter-writing collective for the wrongly convicted. Tamsin signs everything now. Beat: resolution—visibility as homecoming.
